To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
increasing energy expenditure and energy turnover is associated with beneficial effects on insulin action and metabolic health.
Cold exposure increases cellular energy turnover and is associated with beneficial effects on metabolic health.
Increasing energy turnover has beneficial effects in type 2 diabetic subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel interventions that increase energy expenditure, and thereby improve metabolic health.
how the body adapts to cold and how these changes may be used to improve metabolic health.
the development and evaluation of novel interventions that increase energy metabolism and substrate turnover and thereby improve metabolic health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exercise is the preferred strategy for increasing energy turnover and improving metabolic health.
exercise training and cold exposure have beneficial effects on metabolic health, and that these effects are mediated through the activation of energy sensors.
increasing energy turnover is associated with an improvement of insulin sensitivity and that the cellular energy sensors AMPK and SIRT1 may be important mediators of these effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cold exposure and exercise are associated with increased energy metabolism and improved insulin sensitivity, and this effect is mediated by cellular energy sensors.
the effects of cold-induced thermogenesis are mediated by increased substrate turnover and that the underlying mechanisms are linked to the cellular energy sensor AMP-activated protein kinase.
cold induced thermogenesis is a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of type 1 and type 2 diabetes and that this is a novel approach for the treatment of diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cold-induced thermogenesis may be a useful strategy in the treatment of type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
exercise, exercise training, and cold exposure are all effective strategies to increase energy turnover and may be used in combination for the prevention and therapy of type 2 DM.
cold exposure can be used as a non-pharmacological intervention for the prevention and therapy of type 2 Diabetes.
